newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM's party holds lead before elections.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM's party holds lead before elections.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's Liberal Democratic Party (LDS), facing a general election on November 10, maintained its leading position in two opinion polls conducted over the weekend.

The centre-left LDS, senior partner in the coalition government of the past four years, scored an unchanged 11.6 percent in a survey for the newspaper Delo. A poll for the newspaper Dnevniks showed an increase for the LDS to 15.7 percent from 12.7 the weekend before.
The rightist Social Democrats came second with seven percent in Delo and 7.5 in Dnevnik, compared to last weekend's 6.2 and eight percent respectively.
The LDS took a third of the votes in the last general elections in 1992.

The Social Democrats, headed by former Defence Minister Janez Jansa, hope to become the ruling party through a coalition with the rightist People's Party, which scored between five and 5.5 percent in the two opinion polls.
The Christian Democrats, currently in coalition with the LDS, came in third in both surveys with support of 4.2 percent in each.
The United List of Social Democrats, the former communist party, gained 4.2 percent of votes in Delo's poll and 5.8 percent in Dnevnik's.
However, the surveys showed that between 36.8 and 39.3 percent of the country's 1.5 million voters had not yet decided which way to cast their ballots.
